analysis: Jacksonville opened as a 1.5-point underdog and has moved to a 7-7.5 point favorite at every book -- a genuine 9-point swing, not a stale read (cross-checked live against cleatz.com, which shows the same DK -7.5/-108 number and flags the move as real, not news-free steam). The driver is Philadelphia's Friday injury report: RB1 Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and WR1 DeVonta Smith (hamstring) are both OUT, with WR Hollywood Brown (ankle) also OUT -- the Eagles are missing their top rusher and both outside receiving options for a neutral-site game in London. Jalen Hurts himself is available (calf, not a limiting factor). The sim's own injury-adjusted margin (Jaguars by 13.2) is now notably wider than even the market's own 7.5, largely on the strength of the WR-depth stacking penalty for losing two starting-caliber receivers at once.

The total has come down from 44.5 to roughly 41.5-42 across books, which lines up with an offense expected to lean heavily on backfield committee/practice-squad looks and a diminished air attack -- the model's injury-adjusted total (37.1) reads lower still, consistent with a de-fanged Philadelphia passing game, though some of that gap is already priced into the market given how public and well-covered this injury news is (cleatz' prediction-market feeds already show Jacksonville near 76% implied win probability).
